questions.prompt: An authenticator is enabled for an organization. What does that alone establish?

options.text: It is available under the applicable configuration, not enrolled by every user
options.explanation: Availability, enrollment and actual authentication use are separate facts.

options.text: Every user already enrolled it
options.explanation: Organization availability does not establish individual enrollment.

options.text: Every sign-in used it successfully
options.explanation: Use requires evidence from the actual attempt.

options.text: Every application accepts the resulting assurance
options.explanation: App requirements must still be evaluated.

questions.prompt: A user has an active authenticator enrollment. What remains distinct?

options.text: Whether it was successfully used for the current authentication requirement
options.explanation: An enrollment prepares a method but is not a challenge result.

options.text: Whether the enrollment record exists
options.explanation: The question explicitly supplies that fact.

options.text: Whether enrollment and use must have identical timestamps
options.explanation: They are different events and need not coincide.

options.text: Whether every enrolled method meets every policy
options.explanation: Policy requirements can distinguish methods and contexts.

questions.prompt: An enrollment policy requires an authenticator, while an app policy requires authentication assurance. Why distinguish them?

options.text: One governs enrollment readiness; the other governs sign-in requirements
options.explanation: Being enrolled and satisfying a particular attempt's requirement differ.

options.text: Both simply create application accounts
options.explanation: These policies concern authentication readiness and requirements.

options.text: Enrollment automatically grants every app role
options.explanation: Local authorization remains independent.

options.text: An app policy must erase all enrollments
options.explanation: That is not the purpose of an authentication requirement.

questions.prompt: A policy requires multiple factors. Why is entering the same password twice insufficient by itself?

options.text: Repeating one type of proof does not create independent factor categories
options.explanation: MFA depends on the required factor properties, not the number of repeated prompts.

options.text: Any two screens always establish MFA
options.explanation: Screen count is not an assurance definition.

options.text: A longer password automatically becomes a second factor
options.explanation: Credential length does not create another factor category.

options.text: Every application must implement identical methods
options.explanation: Supported requirements and methods vary by policy and integration.

questions.prompt: A user has Okta Verify enrolled. Why should an engineer identify the actual method and policy result?

options.text: Different methods and device/context requirements can matter to assurance
options.explanation: A product name alone does not prove which method satisfied an attempt.

options.text: Every Okta Verify use is identical in assurance and prerequisites
options.explanation: That overgeneralizes supported methods and policy contexts.

options.text: Enrollment proves every later challenge succeeded
options.explanation: The current event still needs its own outcome.

options.text: The app can infer the method from the user's department
options.explanation: Profile department does not establish authentication proof.

questions.prompt: A project wants to rely on FastPass for an app requirement. What should be verified?

options.text: Supported configuration, device/enrollment context and the actual policy outcome
options.explanation: A method label alone does not prove readiness or satisfaction in a particular attempt.

options.text: Assume enabling the org setting enrolls every device
options.explanation: Availability does not establish each user's actual setup.

options.text: Assume a prior password event proves FastPass use
options.explanation: The authentication evidence must identify the relevant method and result.

options.text: Remove app-policy requirements to avoid prompts
options.explanation: That weakens the requirement instead of verifying supported satisfaction.

questions.prompt: An existing provider session does not meet a stronger app requirement and the user is challenged. Is this necessarily a fault?

options.text: No; the additional check can be expected policy enforcement
options.explanation: Session reuse depends on whether existing assurance satisfies the app's requirement.

options.text: Yes; SSO guarantees no future prompts
options.explanation: Single sign-on does not waive all later authentication requirements.

options.text: Yes; every repeated prompt proves a missing app account
options.explanation: A challenge concerns authentication and does not establish account absence.

options.text: No policy evidence is ever needed
options.explanation: The actual selected policy and outcome should still be checked.

questions.prompt: A user is enrolled but cannot complete a current authenticator challenge. What is a useful investigation?

options.text: Identify the enrollment, method, device/context and actual challenge result
options.explanation: Enrollment existence does not explain every current use failure.

options.text: Assume enrollment never occurred
options.explanation: The question supplies an enrollment record.

options.text: Reset all authenticators without inspecting the evidence
options.explanation: A broad reset can be unnecessary and obscure the failed boundary.

options.text: Change the user's app role first
options.explanation: Resource authorization does not repair authentication proof.

questions.prompt: An authorized support process may reset one problematic enrollment. What should guide the scope?

options.text: The actual affected enrollment, identity verification and approved recovery procedure
options.explanation: Recovery actions should fit the demonstrated issue and supported authority.

options.text: Always erase every user's enrollment
options.explanation: That exceeds the supplied individual issue.

options.text: Use a matching display name as sufficient identity proof
options.explanation: Support identity verification needs the approved stronger process.

options.text: Promise every existing app session will end
options.explanation: Enrollment reset does not by itself establish universal session termination.

questions.prompt: An event records successful authenticator enrollment, but no sign-in attempt is supplied. What remains unknown?

options.text: Whether the app's authentication requirement was later satisfied
options.explanation: Enrollment evidence is not a later authentication or target-access result.

options.text: Whether enrollment was recorded as successful
options.explanation: That specific event is supplied.

options.text: Whether an app policy can require assurance
options.explanation: It can; this packet simply lacks its runtime outcome.

options.text: Whether every enrolled user is an administrator
options.explanation: Enrollment conveys no such local role.

questions.reasoning: Before choosing, explain which fact supports your conclusion and what the supplied evidence leaves unknown.
evidence: Current sign-in or target access result: not supplied

questions.prompt: A challenge seems unexpected. What should be checked before changing an authentication rule?

options.text: The actual app-policy association, matching context and selected rule
options.explanation: An apparent prompt problem may reflect correct selection or a genuine selection mismatch.

options.text: Only the user's enrollment count
options.explanation: Count alone does not establish the applicable rule.

options.text: Only a policy with a familiar name
options.explanation: Names do not prove association and rule selection.

options.text: Always weaken the first rule in the list
options.explanation: Changes need the actual selected requirement and intended behavior.

questions.prompt: MFA succeeds but the application rejects the user's local account. Which distinction matters?

options.text: Authentication assurance and application account acceptance are separate
options.explanation: Successful proof does not override a later application eligibility check.

options.text: MFA necessarily failed because access was denied
options.explanation: The stated MFA outcome can remain successful.

options.text: The application must ignore disabled account state
options.explanation: Local account requirements remain applicable.

options.text: Another MFA prompt necessarily creates the missing account
options.explanation: Authentication does not itself perform account provisioning.

questions.reasoning: Before choosing, explain which fact supports your conclusion and what the supplied evidence leaves unknown.
